newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industry sales up 3.72 pct in Jan - CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industry sales up 3.72 pct in Jan - CNI.

text.p: Brazilian industry sales in January rose a seasonally adjusted 3.72 percent from December and were 10.55 percent higher than in January 1996, the private National Industy Confederation (CNI) said.
In real terms, net of inflation, January's industrial sales were 0.83 percent up on December, the CNI said in a statement.
January's performance compensated for lower-than-expected industrial sales in December, it said.
Last month, the CNI reported December's industry sales down a seasonally adjusted 4.44 percent compared with November. In 1996 as a year, sales rose 6.27 percent in real terms from 1995.
"This behaviour, marked by swings and which is atypical, perhaps reflects changes in the seasonal factors affecting end-of-year retailing," the CNI said in its statement announcing January's figures.
"We still cannot affirm that the increase (in January) represents consolidation of a period of faster growth, given than the rise represents principally, December's fall," the statement said.
It also noted that industry sales in January rose in only four of 12 states covered by the CNI's study.
The number of people employed in industry fell a seaonally adjusted 0.69 percent in January from December's levels and was 4.28 percent lower than in January 1996, the statement said.
The total number of hours worked rose a seasonally adjusted 2.58 percent in January from December and was 2.28 percent lower than in January 1996, it said.
Brazilian industry was functioning at a seasonally adjusted average of 78.1 percent of installed capacity, down from 78.9 percent in December and up from 76.2 percent in January 1996.
